The hatchlings, or more precisely the newborn young produced following a gestation that concludes in live birth, emerge fully formed and capable of immediate independent foraging, though they remain vulnerable to predation during their first weeks of life.

Once this milestone is reached, the young lizards begin transitioning from an exclusive focus on growth toward the allocation of resources for reproduction, a shift that carries substantial energetic implications for the remainder of their lives.
